editorial.headline: Tobacco Retail Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans tobacco, smoking accessories, e-cigarettes and e-liquids—open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this retail activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali’s island-wide permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, and this activity falls within that restriction: at the Besar scale, every scope is classified as Low or Medium-Low risk. The block is tied to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026.

The commercial scope is wider than a cigarette counter. It covers retail sales of tobacco in forms including kretek cigarettes, white cigarettes, cigars, clove tobacco cigarettes, loose tobacco, nasal tobacco, and tobacco for pipes or rolling papers. It also includes the retail sale of smoking products and accessories such as lighters, pipes and cigarette-rolling equipment. Electronic cigarettes and e-liquid sit within the same activity, placing conventional tobacco retail and vaping products inside one defined retail scope.

This is an activity for a retailer dealing directly in those products and accessories, rather than a description of a single product format or outlet style. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. Nationally, the investment setting is clear: the activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, under the cited presidential regulations. That national openness, however, does not override the provincial PMA registration block in Bali.

For founders, the important distinction is not semantic but operational. A nationally open activity may still be unavailable for PMA registration in Bali when the provincial moratorium applies. Here, the relevant Bali status is Blocked (risk class) because the recorded Besar-scale risk classification is Low or Medium-Low throughout the activity’s scopes. The national position remains full foreign ownership; the Bali position is that PMA registration is blocked island-wide under the permanent moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali’s island-wide block on PMA registration for this activity.
